conflict_topics: cooking strong-smelling food (sambal) in shared flat
impact on work/clients (video calls) and bedrooms
smell transferring to laundry in service yard
dialogue_quality_notes: Exchanges are concise and pragmatic; participants state personal constraints (work schedule, room location, laundry times) and propose concrete accommodations.
Few repetitive turns; confirmations appear but do not add new content.
Speakers respond directly to each other's proposals (e.g., heads-up, alternate nights), keeping the discussion grounded in practical trade-offs.
evaluation.final_reason: The group negotiated a compromise: Agent B asked for a heads-up before strong-smelling cooking so they can "close my door" (Round 6: "If you just give us a heads-up... I can close my door." / Agent D: "Okay, Agent B, I can do that."). Agent C asked D to avoid Monday/Wednesday/Friday laundry evenings: "I do my laundry on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday evenings. Could you cook it on the other nights?" (Round 7), and Agent D agreed: "Okay. I can cook it on the other nights, then." Agent B confirmed the plan: "Great. So we have a plan." These show D adjusted cooking times and promised notices, while B and C accepted practical accommodations. However Agent A's original request that "nobody cook strong-smelling food in the flat from now on" was not fully accepted; the group settled on a schedule/heads-up rather than a full ban, so some of A's original demand remains unmet.
position_change_notes: Agent D moved from asserting cultural importance of sambal to agreeing to concrete limits: initially accepted 'after 7 p.m. or weekends' (Round 3), later agreed to give B a heads-up (Round 6) and to avoid C's laundry nights (Round 7).
Agent B shifted from raising a complaint to proposing a practical accommodation: asked for a heads-up so they can close their door, and later confirmed the plan (Round 8).
Agent C initially raised the laundry problem and then proposed the specific constraint (avoid Mon/Wed/Fri), which D accepted.

Agent A started with a strict request ('nobody cook strong-smelling food') and offered time-based limits, but did not explicitly accept the final modified plan; A therefore softened the original demand early but did not explicitly confirm the later detailed compromise.

substantive_insights: Tension was primarily between D's regular cultural food and others' practical exposures (work calls, neighboring bedroom, laundry).
Effective solutions combined individual accommodations (B closes door on notice) and scheduling (D avoids specified laundry nights), rather than an absolute ban.
A full ban requested by Agent A was not accepted; the group favored compromises that preserve D's ability to cook while reducing impacts on others.
